Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you altogether?﴾ He said: Do you wish that it be withheld from you, and you did not do what you were commanded?

Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he travelled, would mount his riding beast, then say *Allahu akbar* three times, then say: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿And we could not have subdued it﴾ that he said: "Capable of it" (*mutiqin*).

'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted from him concerning ﴿Is one brought up among ornaments...﴾ that he said: It refers to women. He distinguished between their dress and the dress of men, deprived them of inheritance and testimony, commanded them to remain seated, and named them *al-khawalif* (those who stay behind).

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: I used to read this word: ﴿Who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾, so I asked Ibn 'Abbas, and he said: "Servants of the Most Merciful?" I said: In my copy of the Qur'an it is "with the Most Merciful" (*'inda al-Rahman*). He said: Erase it and write it as "servants of the Most Merciful."

* *

(p-1361) It is a Meccan surah. Al-Qurtubi said: This is the view of all of them. Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that they both said: The surah *Ha-Mim al-Ahqaf* was revealed in Mecca.

Ibn al-Durays and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me the surah of al-Ahqaf, and another man taught it differently from my recitation. I said: Who taught you it? He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me something other than this. So we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and I said: O Messenger of Allah, did you not teach me such-and-such? He said: Yes. And the other said: Did you not teach me such-and-such? He said: Yes. Then the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed, and he said: Let each of you recite what he has heard, for those before you were destroyed only by disagreement."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

His words: 1. ﴿Ha Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ This has already been discussed fully in the surah of Ghafir and what follows it. We mentioned the grammatical analysis (*wajh al-i'rab*) and the explanation of what is the truth: that the opening letters of the surahs belong to the *mutashabih* (the ambiguous verses), whose knowledge must be left to the One who sent it down.

﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾ of all created things, in their entirety, except with truth. This is an exceptive phrase (*istithna' mufarragh*) from the most general of states, that is: except as a creation bound with the truth which the divine will requires. His words ﴿and for a specified term﴾ are coordinated with "the truth": that is, except with the truth, and for a specified term, by supposing an omitted noun: that is, and by appointing a specified term. This term is the Day of Resurrection, when the heavens and the earth and what is between them will come to an end, and the earth will be replaced by another earth and the heavens.

It was said that the specified term means the end of the term of each individual created thing. The first view is preferable. This indicates the Hour's arrival and the termination of the duration of this world, and that Allah did not create His creation in vain and for no purpose, but created it for reward and punishment. ﴿But those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of﴾, that is: from what they were warned and frightened of in the Qur'an, of resurrection, reckoning and recompense; they are turning away, avoiding it, not preparing for it. The clause is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), meaning: while they are turning away from it, not believing in it. The "*ma*" in His words "what they are warned of" may be a relative pronoun, or it may be a verbal-noun (*masdariyyah*) "ma".

﴿Say: Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah?﴾ That is: tell me what you worship besides Allah, of idols. ﴿Show me what they have created of the earth﴾, that is: what thing they created from it. His words "show me" may be an emphasis on His words "have you considered": that is, tell me, show me, and the second object of "have you considered" is "what they created." It may also not be an emphasis, but this may be a case of *tanazu'* (competition between two verbs for one object), since "have you considered" requires a second object and "show me" does too. ﴿Or do they have a partnership in the heavens?﴾ This "or" is the disjunctive *am*, presumed to mean "rather" plus the interrogative hamzah. The meaning: Rather, do they have a partnership with Allah in them? The interrogation is for reproach and rebuke.

﴿Bring me a Book before this﴾. This is a rebuke for them and a demonstration of their inability and incapacity to bring the like of it. The reference in "this" is to the Qur'an, for it has clearly declared the falsehood of association (*shirk*), that Allah is One with no partner, and that the Hour is true with no doubt about it. So is there for the polytheists any book that contradicts this Book, or any proof that opposes this proof?

﴿Or some trace of knowledge﴾. In *al-Sihah*, it is said: "*aw athara min 'ilm*" means a remnant of it, and likewise *al-athrah* with a vowelled *tha'*.

Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, a remnant of the knowledge of the earlier people.

Al-Farra' and al-Mubarrad said: it means what is transmitted from the books of the earlier people.

Al-Wahidi said: This is the meaning of the words of the exegetes.

'Ata' said: or something you transmit from a prophet who came before Muhammad (ﷺ).

Muqatil said: or a narration of knowledge from the prophets.

Al-Zajjaj said: "*aw athara*" means a sign. *Al-athara* is a verbal noun like *al-samahah* (generosity) and *al-shaja'ah* (courage). The root of the word is from *athar* (trace), which is a narration. One says: *athartu al-hadith, uthiruhu, athrah, athara*, and *athran*, when you relate it from another.

The majority read *athara* as a verbal noun, like *al-samahah* and *al-ghawayah* (misguidance). Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, 'Ikrimah, al-Sulami, al-Hasan and Abu Raja' read it with a fatha on the hamzah and the tha', without an alif. Al-Kisa'i read *uthrah* with a damma on the hamzah and a sukun on the tha'.

﴿If you are truthful﴾ in your claim that you make, which is your saying that Allah has a partner. You have brought nothing of this, so the falsity of their statement is established by the rational and transmitted proofs against it.

﴿And who is more astray than one who invokes, besides Allah, those who will not answer him?﴾ That is: there is no one more astray than him, nor more ignorant. For he invokes what does not hear, so how can he hope for an answer, let alone for bringing benefit or repelling harm? Thus it becomes clear that he (p-1362) is the most ignorant of the ignorant and the most astray of the astray. The interrogation is for reproach and rebuke. His words ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾ are the limit of their not answering.

﴿And they are heedless of their invocation﴾. The first pronoun refers to the idols, and the second to their worshippers. The meaning: the idols they invoke are heedless of their invocation of them. They do not hear and do not understand, because they are inanimate objects. The plural in both pronouns is in view of the meaning of "*man*" (whoever). The worshippers of idols applied to the idols what applies to rational beings, because the polytheists believed that the idols understand.

﴿And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and deniers of their worship﴾. That is: when the people who worshipped the idols are gathered, the idols will be enemies to them, disowning one another and cursing one another. It has been said that Allah will create life in the idols, and they will deny them.

It was also said that the meaning is that they deny them and oppose them by the tongue of their state, not by the tongue of speech.

As for the angels, Jesus, 'Uzayr and the devils, they will disown those who worshipped them on the Day of Resurrection, as in His words: ﴿We disown You; they did not used to worship us﴾ [al-Qasas 63]. ﴿And they will be disbelievers in their worship﴾, that is: those who were worshipped by the polytheists would be disbelievers in their worship, that is, deniers and rejecters. It was said that the pronoun in "they will be" refers to the worshippers, as in His words: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am 23]. The first view is preferable.

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them﴾, that is: the verses of the Qur'an, clear in their meanings and manifest in their indications. ﴿Those who disbelieve say of the truth﴾, that is: concerning it and about it, referring to the verses, ﴿when it has come to them﴾, that is: at the time it came to them: ﴿This is manifest magic.﴾ That is: evidently magic.

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ The "or" is the disjunctive *am*: that is, rather, do they say he invented it? The interrogation is for denial and for wonder at their conduct. "Rather" marks a transition from their naming the verses as magic to their saying that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invented what he brought. In this there is reproach and rebuke beyond what needs to be said.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them, so He said: ﴿Say: If I have invented it, then you have no power to avail me anything against Allah.﴾ That is: say, "If I had invented it by way of supposition and assumption, as you claim, you would not be able to ward off Allah's punishment from me. So how would I invent [a lie] against Allah for your sake, when you cannot repel His punishment from me?" ﴿He is most knowing of what you are deep into﴾, that is, what you plunge into of denial. Al-ifada (immersion) in a matter means to plunge into it and rush into it; it is said "afadu fi al-hadith" (they rushed into the talk), and "afada al-ba'ir" (the camel poured out) when it pushed its cud out of its stomach.

The meaning: Allah knows best what you say about the Qur'an and plunge into of denial of it, and of saying that it is sorcery and soothsaying. ﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾, for He bears witness for me that the Qur'an is from Him and that I have conveyed to you, and He bears witness against you of denial and obstinacy. In this is a severe warning. ﴿And He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful﴾ to whoever repents, believes, affirms the Qur'an, and acts upon what is in it. That is: He is abundant in forgiveness and mercy, and perfect in both.

﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾. Al-bid' in everything means the beginning; that is: I am not the first messenger, for Allah has sent many messengers before me.

It is said: al-bid' means al-badi' (the wondrous), like khuff and khafif (light). Al-badi' is that for which no like has been seen, from al-ibtida' which is al-ikhtira' (innovation/origination). A thing is "bid'" with a kasra, meaning mubtada' (originated), and "fulan bid' fi hadha al-amr" means he is unique in this matter. So said al-Akhfash. Qutrub recited:

"I am not a novelty amid the events that befall men, who passed on after Musa and Sa'ada."

'Ikrimah, Abu Haywa and Ibn Abi 'Abla read "bidaan" with a fatha on the dal, on the supposition of an omitted mudaf: that is, "I was not one possessing novelty." Mujahid read it with a fatha on the ba' and a kasra on the dal, as a descriptive. ﴿Nor do I know what will be done with me or with you﴾: that is, what will be done with me in the time to come: will I remain in Makkah or be expelled from it? Will I die or be killed? Will punishment be hastened for you or will you be given respite? This is only in this world.

As for the Hereafter, He has made known that he and his community will be in Paradise, and the disbelievers in the Fire.

It was also said that the meaning is: I do not know what will be done with me or with you on the Day of Resurrection. When this verse was revealed, the polytheists rejoiced and said, "How can we follow a prophet who does not know what will be done with him or with us, and who has no superiority over us?" Then Allah revealed His saying, Most High: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2]. The first view is preferable.

﴿I follow only what is revealed to me﴾. The majority read "yuha" in the passive voice: that is, I follow only the Qur'an and do not innovate anything of my own accord. The meaning is the restriction of his actions, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to revelation, not the restriction of following to revelation.

﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾: that is, I warn you of the punishment of Allah and make you fear His chastisement, in a manner of clarification.

Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh have related, through Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿or a remnant of knowledge﴾, that he said: "The line (of writing)."

Sufyan said: "I know of it only from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace," meaning that the report is marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and not mawquf (stopping at Ibn 'Abbas).

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh have related, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "There was a prophet among the prophets who used to draw lines; whoever happens upon a line like his line, knows (it)." The meaning of this is established in the Sahih, and the people of knowledge have various interpretations of it.

From where do we know that these sandy lines agree with that line? And where is the sound chain of narration to that prophet, or to our Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that this line is in such and such a form? So what the people of sand-divination do is nothing but ignorance and misguidance.

Ibn Mardawayh has related, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, regarding ﴿or a remnant of knowledge﴾, that he said: "Beauty of handwriting."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and al-Hakim have related, through al-Sha'bi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿or a remnant of knowledge﴾, he said: "A line that the Arabs used to draw in the earth."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have related, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿or a remnant of knowledge﴾, that he said: "A clear evidence of the matter."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh have related from him regarding His saying: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾, that he said: "I am not the first of the messengers," ﴿nor do I know what will be done with me or with you﴾. Then Allah revealed after this: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2], and His saying: ﴿that He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens﴾ [al-Fath: 5], and so on, so Allah, glorified is He, informed His Prophet of what will be done with him and with the believers all together.

Abu Dawud, in his al-Nasikh, also related from him that this verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿That Allah may forgive you﴾. It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari and others, from the hadith of Umm al-'Ala', who said: "When 'Uthman ibn Maz'un died, I said: 'May Allah have mercy on you, Abu al-Sa'ib; my testimony upon you is that Allah has honoured you.' The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: 'How do you know that Allah has honoured him? As for him, certainty has come to him from his Lord, and I hope good for him. By Allah, though I am the Messenger of Allah, I do not know what will be done with me or with you.'" Umm al-'Ala' said: "By Allah, I will never again declare anyone pure after him."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 43, verses 1–12 (part 1 of 3):

Al-Qurtubi said: It is Meccan by consensus. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Surat Ḥā Mīm al-Zukhruf was revealed in Mecca." Muqatil said: "Except His words: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45], meaning that it was revealed in Medina."

(p-1335) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His words: ﴿Ḥā Mīm. By the Clear Book﴾. The discussion here regarding i'rab (grammatical analysis) is like the discussion we presented regarding ﴿Yā Sīn. By the Wise Qur'an﴾. If Ḥā Mīm is taken as an oath, then the wāw is conjunctive; if it is not taken as an oath, then the wāw is for swearing.

The response to the oath is ﴿Indeed, We have made it﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever makes the response to "wal-Kitāb" to be Ḥā Mīm, as you say: "He descended, by Allah," "It was obligatory, by Allah," then he stops at "al-Kitāb al-Mubīn." The meaning of "jaʿalnāhu" (We have made it) is: We named it and described it; for this reason it transitively takes two objects. Al-Suddi said: the meaning is: We sent it down as a Qur'an. Mujahid said: We said it. Sufyan al-Thawri said: We made it clear in Arabic. Al-Zajjaj likewise said: it was sent down in the language of the Arabs, because every prophet's scripture was sent down in the language of his people. Muqatil said: because the language of the people of Paradise is Arabic. ﴿So that you may understand﴾: that is, We made that Book a Qur'an in Arabic so that you may comprehend it, understand its meanings, and encompass what is in it. Ibn Zayd said: "so that you may reflect."

﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book﴾: that is, indeed the Qur'an is in the Preserved Tablet with Us, that is, with Us ﴿exalted, full of wisdom﴾: elevated in rank, firm in its arrangement, in which there is no discrepancy or contradiction. The sentence is either a conjunction with the sentence sworn by, falling under the meaning of the oath, or a resumed sentence confirming what precedes it.

Al-Zajjaj said: "Umm al-Kitāb" is the origin of the Book, and the origin of everything is its umm (mother). The Qur'an is recorded with Allah in the Preserved Tablet, as He said: ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an, in a preserved tablet﴾ [al-Buruj: 21–22]. Ibn Jurayj said: what is meant by His words "and indeed it" is the deeds of creation, of faith and disbelief, obedience and disobedience.

Qatada said: He informs of its station, its nobility, and its virtue: that is, if you deny it, O people of Mecca, then it is with Us noble, elevated, and firm, protected from falsehood.

﴿Shall We then withhold the reminder from you, turning away?﴾ It is said: "ḍaraba ʿannahu" and "aḍraba ʿannahu" when one leaves it and refrains from it; so said al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj and others. The accusative of "ṣafḥan" is as a verbal noun (maṣdar), and it was said: it is in the accusative of circumstance, meaning: "Shall We withhold the reminder from you while turning away?" The ṣafḥ is the verbal noun of their saying: "ṣafaḥtu ʿanhu" when I turned away from him, because you turn to him the side of your face and neck. The "dhikr" here means the Qur'an, and the interrogation is for denial and rebuke.

Al-Kisa'i said: the meaning is: "Shall We fold up the reminder from you," meaning: "so that you will not be admonished nor commanded."

Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: "Shall We withhold the punishment from you and not punish you for your excess and your disbelief?" Qatada said: the meaning is: "Shall We destroy you and not command you or forbid you?" It is narrated from him that he said: the meaning is: "Shall We refrain from sending down the Qur'an because you do not believe in it?"

It was said: "al-dhikr" means "admonition" (tadhkir), as if He said: "Shall We leave off admonishing you ﴿because you are a people who are excessive﴾" — Nafi', Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "in kuntum" with a kasra on "in," as the conditional particle, with the response omitted, the preceding context indicating it. The rest read it with a fatḥa on it, as a causal particle, meaning: "because you were a people immersed in excess and persistent in it." Abu ʿUbayd chose the reading with fatḥa.

Then He consoled His Messenger (ﷺ) and said: ﴿And how many a prophet We sent among the earlier peoples﴾. "Kam" here is the informative "kam," whose meaning is multiplication: how much We sent of prophets among the earlier nations.

﴿And there came not to them a prophet but they used to mock him﴾, like the mockery of your people toward you.

﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might﴾: that is, We destroyed a people stronger in power than these people. "Baṭshan" is in the accusative as a specification or circumstance, meaning: seizing (with might). ﴿And the example of the former peoples has passed on﴾: that is, their mention has preceded in the Qur'an more than once. Qatada said: "their punishment." It was said: "their description," and "mathal" means description and report.

In this is a severe threat, for it implies that the earlier peoples were destroyed for denying the messengers, and these, if they persist in denying you and disbelieving in what you have brought, will be destroyed like them.

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "They were created by the Mighty, the All-Knowing"﴾: that is, if you asked these disbelievers of your people who created these upper and lower bodies, they would acknowledge that Allah is their Creator and would not deny it. That is worse for their state and more severe for their punishment, because they worshipped some of Allah's creatures and made them partners to Him, indeed they resorted to what neither hears, nor sees, nor benefits, nor harms, of creatures, namely idols, and made them partners of Allah.

Then He described Himself with what indicates the greatness of His blessing upon His servants and the perfection of His power in His creatures, and said: ﴿Who made the earth a cradle for you﴾. This is a new statement, not connected to what precedes it; for if it were connected to the words of the disbelievers, they would have said: "Who made the earth a cradle for us." "Mihad" means bed and carpet, and its explanation has already preceded. Al-Jumhur read "mihādan," and the Kufans read "mahdan." ﴿And made for you therein pathways﴾: that is, roads you travel to wherever you wish; it was said: means of livelihood by which you live. ﴿That you may be guided﴾ by traveling them to your goals and benefits.

﴿And who sends down from the sky water in measure﴾: that is, in the measure of need and as the benefit requires, and He did not send down upon you from it more than your need, so that it would destroy your crops, demolish your dwellings, and drown you, nor less than it, so that you would need more; and in accordance with what His will requires regarding the provision of His servants, by expanding at times and restricting at others. ﴿And We revived thereby a dead land﴾: that is, We gave life by that water to a land barren of vegetation.

Al-Jumhur read "maytan" with a light pronunciation. ʿIsa and Abu Jaʿfar read it with shadda.

﴿Thus you will be brought forth﴾ from your graves: that is, like that revival of the land by bringing forth its plants after there was no vegetation in it, you will be raised from your graves living; for He who is able to do this is able to do that. The explanation of this has passed in Al ʿImran and al-Aʿraf.

Al-Jumhur read "tukhrajūn" in the passive voice, while al-Aʿmash, Yahya ibn Wathhab, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Ibn Dhakwan on the authority of Ibn ʿAmir read it in the active voice.

﴿And who created all the pairs﴾: what is meant by "azwāj" here is kinds. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: all the kinds.

Al-Hasan said: winter and summer, night and day, heavens and earth, Paradise and Hellfire. It was said: pairs of animals, male and female. It was said: pairs of plants, as in His saying: ﴿And We caused to grow therein every beautiful pair﴾ [Qaf: 7] and ﴿of every noble pair﴾ [al-Shuʿara': 7; Luqman: 10]. It was said: what man turns over in of good and evil, faith and disbelief. The first is preferable.

﴿And made for you of the ships and cattle that which you ride﴾, at sea and on land: that is, what you ride.

﴿That you may sit firmly upon their backs﴾: the pronoun refers to what Abu ʿUbayd mentioned. Al-Farra' said: He attributed the "backs" to a singular because what is meant is the genus, so the singular became in meaning the plural, like the genus; therefore it was mentioned, and "ẓahr" was pluralized because what is meant is the backs of this genus. "Istiwāʾ" means elevation: that is, that you may be elevated upon the backs of what you ride of ships and cattle. ﴿Then you remember the favor of your Lord when you are settled upon them﴾: that is, this blessing which He bestowed upon you, the subjugation of that vehicle at sea and on land.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it is that one says: "Praise be to Allah, who provided me with this and carried me upon it." ﴿And say, "Exalted is He who has subjected this to us"﴾: that is, He made this vehicle submissive to us. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib read: "Exalted is He who subjected this to us."

Qatada said: He has taught you how to say when you ride.

The meaning of ﴿And we were not able to control it﴾ is: we were not capable of it. It is said: "aqrana hadhā al-baʿīr" when he was able to control it. Al-Akhfash and Abu ʿUbayda said: "muqrinīn" means controlling. It was said: equal to it in strength, from their saying: "he is the qirn of so-and-so" when he is like him in strength. Qutrub recited the verse of ʿAmr ibn Maʿdi Karib:

"Indeed the tribes know that ʿUqayl has for us, in calamities, none who controls us."

Another said:

"You rode the two difficult mounts of recklessness and cowardice, and you are not ones who can master the difficult."

The meaning of "al-anʿam" here is camels specifically; it was said: camels and cattle, and the first is preferable.

﴿And indeed to our Lord we will surely return﴾: that is, we will return to Him. This is the completion of what is said upon mounting a beast or a ship.

Then He returned — glory be to Him — to mention the disbelievers who were previously mentioned, and said: ﴿And they have attributed to Him from His servants a portion﴾. Qatada said: that is, an equal, meaning whatever is worshipped besides Allah.

Al-Zajjaj and al-Mubarrad said: "al-juzʾ" here means daughters, and "al-juzʾ" among the people of Arabic means daughters; it is said: "qad ajza'at al-mar'a" when the woman bore daughters. From it is the saying of the poet:

"If a free woman has given birth to daughters one day, there is no wonder; a free woman may sometimes bear males, sometimes the opposite."

The author of al-Kashshaf considered explaining "al-juzʾ" as daughters to be among the innovations of tafsir, and declared it a lie upon the Arabs.

This can be answered: al-Zajjaj and al-Mubarrad narrated it, and they are the two imams of the Arabic language, its preservers, and the ultimate authorities in knowledge of it. And what will come later supports explaining "al-juzʾ" as daughters, His saying: ﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates?﴾, and His saying: ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful﴾, and His saying: ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾. It was also said: what is meant by "al-juzʾ" here is the angels, for they made them children of Allah, glory be to Him; this was said by Mujahid and al-Hasan.

Al-Azhari said: the meaning of the verse is that they made for Allah a portion of His servants, meaning: they made Allah's share of offspring. ﴿Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful﴾: that is, manifestly ungrateful and exaggerated in it. It was said: what is meant by "al-insān" here is the disbeliever, for he is the one who denies Allah's blessings upon him with clear denial.

Then He denounced them for this, saying: ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen for you sons?﴾ This is an interrogation of reproach and rebuke.

"Am" here is the disjunctive "am," and the meaning is: has your Lord taken daughters for Himself, and chosen sons for you? So He made for Himself the lesser of the two categories, and for you the more excellent of them. It is said: "aṣfaytuhu bi-kadhā," meaning: I preferred him with it; and "aṣfaytuhu al-wudd," meaning: I made the affection pure for him. Similar to this verse is His saying: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That would be an unjust division﴾ [al-Najm: 21], and His saying: ﴿Has your Lord then chosen you with sons?﴾ [al-Isra': 40]. The clause "wa-aṣfākum" is conjoined to "ittakhadha," and falls with it under the denial.

Then He increased their reproach and rebuke, saying: ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as an example﴾: that is, of what He ascribed to the Most Merciful, glory be to Him, of having taken daughters for Himself. The meaning is that when one of them is given good news that a daughter has been born to him, he is grieved by it and its effect appears on him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿his face becomes dark﴾, that is, his face becomes black because of the birth of a female to him, when what was born to him was not a male in its place. ﴿And he is filled with suppressed grief﴾: that is, intensely grieving, greatly distressed, full of it.

Qatada said: "grieved." ʿIkrimah said: "distressed." It was said: "silent." The clause ﴿and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾ is in the place of accusative as a circumstance.

Then He increased their reproach and rebuke, saying: ﴿Is one who is brought up in ornaments, and who in dispute is not clear?﴾ The meaning of "yunashsha'" is "yurabbā" (is raised), and "al-nushū'" is upbringing, and "al-ḥilya" is adornment. The "man" is in the accusative place by an implied governing verb conjoined to "ja'alū," and the meaning is: "Did they make for Him — glory be to Him — one who is raised in adornment, while he is incapable of managing his own affairs, and when he is disputed with, he cannot establish his argument or repel what his opponent argues against him, due to deficiency of intellect and weakness of judgment?"

Al-Mubarrad said: the estimated sense of the verse is: "Or do they attribute to Him one who grows up in adornment," meaning: one who grows in ornament.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read *yunsha'u* with a fatha on the *ya'* and a sukun on the *nun*. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, Ibn Wathhab, Hafs, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with a damma on the *ya'*, a fatha on the *nun* and a shaddah on the *shin*.

Abu Hatim preferred the first reading (*qira'ah*, recitation), and Abu 'Ubayd preferred the second.

Al-Harawi said: On the first reading the verb is intransitive (*lazim*), and on the second it is transitive (*muta'addin*). The meaning is: she is brought up and grows up among ornaments (*al-hilyah*).

Qatadah said: "A woman rarely speaks with her argument without speaking with the argument against herself." Ibn Zayd and al-Dahhak said: What is "brought up among ornaments" refers to their idols, which they fashioned from gold and silver.

﴿And they made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females.﴾ The word *ja'l* (making, or ascribing) here means saying and passing a judgment on a thing, as when you say: "I made Zayd the best of people," meaning: you said this and judged him to be so.

The Kufans read *'ibad* (servants) in the plural, and Ibn 'Abbas also read it this way. The rest read *'inda al-Rahman* (with the Most Merciful), with a sukun on the *nun*. Abu 'Ubayd preferred the first reading, because the chain of attribution (*al-isnad*) is higher in it, and because Allah only refuted them in their statement that they are the daughters of Allah (p-1337), so He informed them that they are His servants. This reading is supported by His words: ﴿Rather, they are honoured servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26]. Abu Hatim preferred the second reading and said: Confirmation of this reading is His words: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ [al-A'raf 206].

Then He rebuked and reproached them, saying: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ That is, were they present at Allah's creation of them? This is from *shahadah* in the sense of presence (*huduur*). In this there is mockery of them and a declaration of their ignorance.

The majority read *ashahidu* as an interrogative without a waw. Nafi' read *awa-shahidu* (with a waw).

The majority read *satuktabu shahadatuhum* (their testimony will be recorded), with a damma on the *ta'* and the verb in the passive, and *shahadatuhum* in the nominative. Al-Sulami, Ibn al-Sumayfa' and Hubayrah from Hafs read it with a *nun* and the verb in the active, with *shahadatahum* in the accusative. Abu Raja' read *shahadatuhum* in the plural. The meaning: We shall record this testimony that they gave in the register of their deeds, so that We may recompense them for it, and they will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And they said: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them."﴾ This is another kind of their disbelief in Allah, which they brought out for mockery and ridicule. Its meaning: If the Most Merciful had willed, in your supposition, we would not have worshipped these angels. This is a true statement by which falsehood is intended, and its explanation has already passed in al-An'am. Then He, glory be to Him, exposed their ignorance by His words: ﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾, that is: they have no knowledge of what they said, that if Allah willed that they not worship the angels, they would not have worshipped them. Rather, they spoke of it out of ignorance, intending by what has the form of truth something false, and they supposed that whatever He wills, He is pleased with.

Then He made clear the absence of their knowledge by His words: ﴿They are only guessing﴾, that is: they are only lying in what they said, and fabricating a vain excuse.

It was said that the reference in His words "that" (*dhalika*) is to His words: ﴿And they made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females.﴾ This was said by Qatadah, Muqatil and al-Kalbi. Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: That is, they have no knowledge concerning the worship of idols.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The first thing Allah created was the pen, and He commanded it to write what will be until the Day of Resurrection, and the Book is with Him. Then he recited: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you altogether?﴾ He said: Do you wish that it be withheld from you, and you did not do what you were commanded?

Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he travelled, would mount his riding beast, then say *Allahu akbar* three times, then say: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿And we could not have subdued it﴾ that he said: "Capable of it" (*mutiqin*).

'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted from him concerning ﴿Is one brought up among ornaments...﴾ that he said: It refers to women. He distinguished between their dress and the dress of men, deprived them of inheritance and testimony, commanded them to remain seated, and named them *al-khawalif* (those who stay behind).

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: I used to read this word: ﴿Who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾, so I asked Ibn 'Abbas, and he said: "Servants of the Most Merciful?" I said: In my copy of the Qur'an it is "with the Most Merciful" (*'inda al-Rahman*). He said: Erase it and write it as "servants of the Most Merciful."

* *

(p-1361) It is a Meccan surah. Al-Qurtubi said: This is the view of all of them. Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that they both said: The surah *Ha-Mim al-Ahqaf* was revealed in Mecca.

Ibn al-Durays and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me the surah of al-Ahqaf, and another man taught it differently from my recitation. I said: Who taught you it? He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me something other than this. So we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and I said: O Messenger of Allah, did you not teach me such-and-such? He said: Yes. And the other said: Did you not teach me such-and-such? He said: Yes. Then the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed, and he said: Let each of you recite what he has heard, for those before you were destroyed only by disagreement."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

His words: 1. ﴿Ha Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ This has already been discussed fully in the surah of Ghafir and what follows it. We mentioned the grammatical analysis (*wajh al-i'rab*) and the explanation of what is the truth: that the opening letters of the surahs belong to the *mutashabih* (the ambiguous verses), whose knowledge must be left to the One who sent it down.

﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾ of all created things, in their entirety, except with truth. This is an exceptive phrase (*istithna' mufarragh*) from the most general of states, that is: except as a creation bound with the truth which the divine will requires. His words ﴿and for a specified term﴾ are coordinated with "the truth": that is, except with the truth, and for a specified term, by supposing an omitted noun: that is, and by appointing a specified term. This term is the Day of Resurrection, when the heavens and the earth and what is between them will come to an end, and the earth will be replaced by another earth and the heavens.

It was said that the specified term means the end of the term of each individual created thing. The first view is preferable. This indicates the Hour's arrival and the termination of the duration of this world, and that Allah did not create His creation in vain and for no purpose, but created it for reward and punishment. ﴿But those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of﴾, that is: from what they were warned and frightened of in the Qur'an, of resurrection, reckoning and recompense; they are turning away, avoiding it, not preparing for it. The clause is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), meaning: while they are turning away from it, not believing in it. The "*ma*" in His words "what they are warned of" may be a relative pronoun, or it may be a verbal-noun (*masdariyyah*) "ma".

﴿Say: Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah?﴾ That is: tell me what you worship besides Allah, of idols. ﴿Show me what they have created of the earth﴾, that is: what thing they created from it. His words "show me" may be an emphasis on His words "have you considered": that is, tell me, show me, and the second object of "have you considered" is "what they created." It may also not be an emphasis, but this may be a case of *tanazu'* (competition between two verbs for one object), since "have you considered" requires a second object and "show me" does too. ﴿Or do they have a partnership in the heavens?﴾ This "or" is the disjunctive *am*, presumed to mean "rather" plus the interrogative hamzah. The meaning: Rather, do they have a partnership with Allah in them? The interrogation is for reproach and rebuke.

﴿Bring me a Book before this﴾. This is a rebuke for them and a demonstration of their inability and incapacity to bring the like of it. The reference in "this" is to the Qur'an, for it has clearly declared the falsehood of association (*shirk*), that Allah is One with no partner, and that the Hour is true with no doubt about it. So is there for the polytheists any book that contradicts this Book, or any proof that opposes this proof?

﴿Or some trace of knowledge﴾. In *al-Sihah*, it is said: "*aw athara min 'ilm*" means a remnant of it, and likewise *al-athrah* with a vowelled *tha'*.

Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, a remnant of the knowledge of the earlier people.

Al-Farra' and al-Mubarrad said: it means what is transmitted from the books of the earlier people.

Al-Wahidi said: This is the meaning of the words of the exegetes.

'Ata' said: or something you transmit from a prophet who came before Muhammad (ﷺ).

Muqatil said: or a narration of knowledge from the prophets.

Al-Zajjaj said: "*aw athara*" means a sign. *Al-athara* is a verbal noun like *al-samahah* (generosity) and *al-shaja'ah* (courage). The root of the word is from *athar* (trace), which is a narration. One says: *athartu al-hadith, uthiruhu, athrah, athara*, and *athran*, when you relate it from another.

The majority read *athara* as a verbal noun, like *al-samahah* and *al-ghawayah* (misguidance). Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, 'Ikrimah, al-Sulami, al-Hasan and Abu Raja' read it with a fatha on the hamzah and the tha', without an alif. Al-Kisa'i read *uthrah* with a damma on the hamzah and a sukun on the tha'.

﴿If you are truthful﴾ in your claim that you make, which is your saying that Allah has a partner. You have brought nothing of this, so the falsity of their statement is established by the rational and transmitted proofs against it.

﴿And who is more astray than one who invokes, besides Allah, those who will not answer him?﴾ That is: there is no one more astray than him, nor more ignorant. For he invokes what does not hear, so how can he hope for an answer, let alone for bringing benefit or repelling harm? Thus it becomes clear that he (p-1362) is the most ignorant of the ignorant and the most astray of the astray. The interrogation is for reproach and rebuke. His words ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾ are the limit of their not answering.

﴿And they are heedless of their invocation﴾. The first pronoun refers to the idols, and the second to their worshippers. The meaning: the idols they invoke are heedless of their invocation of them. They do not hear and do not understand, because they are inanimate objects. The plural in both pronouns is in view of the meaning of "*man*" (whoever). The worshippers of idols applied to the idols what applies to rational beings, because the polytheists believed that the idols understand.

﴿And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and deniers of their worship﴾. That is: when the people who worshipped the idols are gathered, the idols will be enemies to them, disowning one another and cursing one another. It has been said that Allah will create life in the idols, and they will deny them.

It was also said that the meaning is that they deny them and oppose them by the tongue of their state, not by the tongue of speech.

As for the angels, Jesus, 'Uzayr and the devils, they will disown those who worshipped them on the Day of Resurrection, as in His words: ﴿We disown You; they did not used to worship us﴾ [al-Qasas 63]. ﴿And they will be disbelievers in their worship﴾, that is: those who were worshipped by the polytheists would be disbelievers in their worship, that is, deniers and rejecters. It was said that the pronoun in "they will be" refers to the worshippers, as in His words: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am 23]. The first view is preferable.

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them﴾, that is: the verses of the Qur'an, clear in their meanings and manifest in their indications. ﴿Those who disbelieve say of the truth﴾, that is: concerning it and about it, referring to the verses, ﴿when it has come to them﴾, that is: at the time it came to them: ﴿This is manifest magic.﴾ That is: evidently magic.

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ The "or" is the disjunctive *am*: that is, rather, do they say he invented it? The interrogation is for denial and for wonder at their conduct. "Rather" marks a transition from their naming the verses as magic to their saying that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invented what he brought. In this there is reproach and rebuke beyond what needs to be said.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them, so He said: ﴿Say: If I have invented it, then you have no power to avail me anything against Allah.﴾ That is: say, "If I had invented it by way of supposition and assumption, as you claim, you would not be able to ward off Allah's punishment from me. So how would I invent [a lie] against Allah for your sake, when you cannot repel His punishment from me?" ﴿He is most knowing of what you are deep into﴾, that is, what you plunge into of denial. Al-ifada (immersion) in a matter means to plunge into it and rush into it; it is said "afadu fi al-hadith" (they rushed into the talk), and "afada al-ba'ir" (the camel poured out) when it pushed its cud out of its stomach.

The meaning: Allah knows best what you say about the Qur'an and plunge into of denial of it, and of saying that it is sorcery and soothsaying. ﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾, for He bears witness for me that the Qur'an is from Him and that I have conveyed to you, and He bears witness against you of denial and obstinacy. In this is a severe warning. ﴿And He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful﴾ to whoever repents, believes, affirms the Qur'an, and acts upon what is in it. That is: He is abundant in forgiveness and mercy, and perfect in both.

﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾. Al-bid' in everything means the beginning; that is: I am not the first messenger, for Allah has sent many messengers before me.

It is said: al-bid' means al-badi' (the wondrous), like khuff and khafif (light). Al-badi' is that for which no like has been seen, from al-ibtida' which is al-ikhtira' (innovation/origination). A thing is "bid'" with a kasra, meaning mubtada' (originated), and "fulan bid' fi hadha al-amr" means he is unique in this matter. So said al-Akhfash. Qutrub recited:

"I am not a novelty amid the events that befall men, who passed on after Musa and Sa'ada."

'Ikrimah, Abu Haywa and Ibn Abi 'Abla read "bidaan" with a fatha on the dal, on the supposition of an omitted mudaf: that is, "I was not one possessing novelty." Mujahid read it with a fatha on the ba' and a kasra on the dal, as a descriptive. ﴿Nor do I know what will be done with me or with you﴾: that is, what will be done with me in the time to come: will I remain in Makkah or be expelled from it? Will I die or be killed? Will punishment be hastened for you or will you be given respite? This is only in this world.

As for the Hereafter, He has made known that he and his community will be in Paradise, and the disbelievers in the Fire.

It was also said that the meaning is: I do not know what will be done with me or with you on the Day of Resurrection. When this verse was revealed, the polytheists rejoiced and said, "How can we follow a prophet who does not know what will be done with him or with us, and who has no superiority over us?" Then Allah revealed His saying, Most High: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2]. The first view is preferable.

﴿I follow only what is revealed to me﴾. The majority read "yuha" in the passive voice: that is, I follow only the Qur'an and do not innovate anything of my own accord. The meaning is the restriction of his actions, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to revelation, not the restriction of following to revelation.

﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾: that is, I warn you of the punishment of Allah and make you fear His chastisement, in a manner of clarification.

Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh have related, through Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿or a remnant of knowledge﴾, that he said: "The line (of writing)."

Sufyan said: "I know of it only from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace," meaning that the report is marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and not mawquf (stopping at Ibn 'Abbas).

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh have related, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "There was a prophet among the prophets who used to draw lines; whoever happens upon a line like his line, knows (it)." The meaning of this is established in the Sahih, and the people of knowledge have various interpretations of it.

From where do we know that these sandy lines agree with that line? And where is the sound chain of narration to that prophet, or to our Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that this line is in such and such a form? So what the people of sand-divination do is nothing but ignorance and misguidance.

Ibn Mardawayh has related, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, regarding ﴿or a remnant of knowledge﴾, that he said: "Beauty of handwriting."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and al-Hakim have related, through al-Sha'bi, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿or a remnant of knowledge﴾, he said: "A line that the Arabs used to draw in the earth."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have related, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿or a remnant of knowledge﴾, that he said: "A clear evidence of the matter."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh have related from him regarding His saying: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾, that he said: "I am not the first of the messengers," ﴿nor do I know what will be done with me or with you﴾. Then Allah revealed after this: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2], and His saying: ﴿that He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens﴾ [al-Fath: 5], and so on, so Allah, glorified is He, informed His Prophet of what will be done with him and with the believers all together.

Abu Dawud, in his al-Nasikh, also related from him that this verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿That Allah may forgive you﴾. It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari and others, from the hadith of Umm al-'Ala', who said: "When 'Uthman ibn Maz'un died, I said: 'May Allah have mercy on you, Abu al-Sa'ib; my testimony upon you is that Allah has honoured you.' The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: 'How do you know that Allah has honoured him? As for him, certainty has come to him from his Lord, and I hope good for him. By Allah, though I am the Messenger of Allah, I do not know what will be done with me or with you.'" Umm al-'Ala' said: "By Allah, I will never again declare anyone pure after him."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 43, verses 1–12 (part 1 of 3):

Al-Qurtubi said: It is Meccan by consensus. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Surat Ḥā Mīm al-Zukhruf was revealed in Mecca." Muqatil said: "Except His words: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45], meaning that it was revealed in Medina."

(p-1335) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His words: ﴿Ḥā Mīm. By the Clear Book﴾. The discussion here regarding i'rab (grammatical analysis) is like the discussion we presented regarding ﴿Yā Sīn. By the Wise Qur'an﴾. If Ḥā Mīm is taken as an oath, then the wāw is conjunctive; if it is not taken as an oath, then the wāw is for swearing.

The response to the oath is ﴿Indeed, We have made it﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever makes the response to "wal-Kitāb" to be Ḥā Mīm, as you say: "He descended, by Allah," "It was obligatory, by Allah," then he stops at "al-Kitāb al-Mubīn." The meaning of "jaʿalnāhu" (We have made it) is: We named it and described it; for this reason it transitively takes two objects. Al-Suddi said: the meaning is: We sent it down as a Qur'an. Mujahid said: We said it. Sufyan al-Thawri said: We made it clear in Arabic. Al-Zajjaj likewise said: it was sent down in the language of the Arabs, because every prophet's scripture was sent down in the language of his people. Muqatil said: because the language of the people of Paradise is Arabic. ﴿So that you may understand﴾: that is, We made that Book a Qur'an in Arabic so that you may comprehend it, understand its meanings, and encompass what is in it. Ibn Zayd said: "so that you may reflect."

﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book﴾: that is, indeed the Qur'an is in the Preserved Tablet with Us, that is, with Us ﴿exalted, full of wisdom﴾: elevated in rank, firm in its arrangement, in which there is no discrepancy or contradiction. The sentence is either a conjunction with the sentence sworn by, falling under the meaning of the oath, or a resumed sentence confirming what precedes it.

Al-Zajjaj said: "Umm al-Kitāb" is the origin of the Book, and the origin of everything is its umm (mother). The Qur'an is recorded with Allah in the Preserved Tablet, as He said: ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an, in a preserved tablet﴾ [al-Buruj: 21–22]. Ibn Jurayj said: what is meant by His words "and indeed it" is the deeds of creation, of faith and disbelief, obedience and disobedience.

Qatada said: He informs of its station, its nobility, and its virtue: that is, if you deny it, O people of Mecca, then it is with Us noble, elevated, and firm, protected from falsehood.

﴿Shall We then withhold the reminder from you, turning away?﴾ It is said: "ḍaraba ʿannahu" and "aḍraba ʿannahu" when one leaves it and refrains from it; so said al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj and others. The accusative of "ṣafḥan" is as a verbal noun (maṣdar), and it was said: it is in the accusative of circumstance, meaning: "Shall We withhold the reminder from you while turning away?" The ṣafḥ is the verbal noun of their saying: "ṣafaḥtu ʿanhu" when I turned away from him, because you turn to him the side of your face and neck. The "dhikr" here means the Qur'an, and the interrogation is for denial and rebuke.

Al-Kisa'i said: the meaning is: "Shall We fold up the reminder from you," meaning: "so that you will not be admonished nor commanded."

Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: "Shall We withhold the punishment from you and not punish you for your excess and your disbelief?" Qatada said: the meaning is: "Shall We destroy you and not command you or forbid you?" It is narrated from him that he said: the meaning is: "Shall We refrain from sending down the Qur'an because you do not believe in it?"

It was said: "al-dhikr" means "admonition" (tadhkir), as if He said: "Shall We leave off admonishing you ﴿because you are a people who are excessive﴾" — Nafi', Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "in kuntum" with a kasra on "in," as the conditional particle, with the response omitted, the preceding context indicating it. The rest read it with a fatḥa on it, as a causal particle, meaning: "because you were a people immersed in excess and persistent in it." Abu ʿUbayd chose the reading with fatḥa.

Then He consoled His Messenger (ﷺ) and said: ﴿And how many a prophet We sent among the earlier peoples﴾. "Kam" here is the informative "kam," whose meaning is multiplication: how much We sent of prophets among the earlier nations.

﴿And there came not to them a prophet but they used to mock him﴾, like the mockery of your people toward you.

﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might﴾: that is, We destroyed a people stronger in power than these people. "Baṭshan" is in the accusative as a specification or circumstance, meaning: seizing (with might). ﴿And the example of the former peoples has passed on﴾: that is, their mention has preceded in the Qur'an more than once. Qatada said: "their punishment." It was said: "their description," and "mathal" means description and report.

In this is a severe threat, for it implies that the earlier peoples were destroyed for denying the messengers, and these, if they persist in denying you and disbelieving in what you have brought, will be destroyed like them.

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "They were created by the Mighty, the All-Knowing"﴾: that is, if you asked these disbelievers of your people who created these upper and lower bodies, they would acknowledge that Allah is their Creator and would not deny it. That is worse for their state and more severe for their punishment, because they worshipped some of Allah's creatures and made them partners to Him, indeed they resorted to what neither hears, nor sees, nor benefits, nor harms, of creatures, namely idols, and made them partners of Allah.

Then He described Himself with what indicates the greatness of His blessing upon His servants and the perfection of His power in His creatures, and said: ﴿Who made the earth a cradle for you﴾. This is a new statement, not connected to what precedes it; for if it were connected to the words of the disbelievers, they would have said: "Who made the earth a cradle for us." "Mihad" means bed and carpet, and its explanation has already preceded. Al-Jumhur read "mihādan," and the Kufans read "mahdan." ﴿And made for you therein pathways﴾: that is, roads you travel to wherever you wish; it was said: means of livelihood by which you live. ﴿That you may be guided﴾ by traveling them to your goals and benefits.

﴿And who sends down from the sky water in measure﴾: that is, in the measure of need and as the benefit requires, and He did not send down upon you from it more than your need, so that it would destroy your crops, demolish your dwellings, and drown you, nor less than it, so that you would need more; and in accordance with what His will requires regarding the provision of His servants, by expanding at times and restricting at others. ﴿And We revived thereby a dead land﴾: that is, We gave life by that water to a land barren of vegetation.

Al-Jumhur read "maytan" with a light pronunciation. ʿIsa and Abu Jaʿfar read it with shadda.

﴿Thus you will be brought forth﴾ from your graves: that is, like that revival of the land by bringing forth its plants after there was no vegetation in it, you will be raised from your graves living; for He who is able to do this is able to do that. The explanation of this has passed in Al ʿImran and al-Aʿraf.

Al-Jumhur read "tukhrajūn" in the passive voice, while al-Aʿmash, Yahya ibn Wathhab, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Ibn Dhakwan on the authority of Ibn ʿAmir read it in the active voice.

﴿And who created all the pairs﴾: what is meant by "azwāj" here is kinds. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: all the kinds.

Al-Hasan said: winter and summer, night and day, heavens and earth, Paradise and Hellfire. It was said: pairs of animals, male and female. It was said: pairs of plants, as in His saying: ﴿And We caused to grow therein every beautiful pair﴾ [Qaf: 7] and ﴿of every noble pair﴾ [al-Shuʿara': 7; Luqman: 10]. It was said: what man turns over in of good and evil, faith and disbelief. The first is preferable.

﴿And made for you of the ships and cattle that which you ride﴾, at sea and on land: that is, what you ride.

﴿That you may sit firmly upon their backs﴾: the pronoun refers to what Abu ʿUbayd mentioned. Al-Farra' said: He attributed the "backs" to a singular because what is meant is the genus, so the singular became in meaning the plural, like the genus; therefore it was mentioned, and "ẓahr" was pluralized because what is meant is the backs of this genus. "Istiwāʾ" means elevation: that is, that you may be elevated upon the backs of what you ride of ships and cattle. ﴿Then you remember the favor of your Lord when you are settled upon them﴾: that is, this blessing which He bestowed upon you, the subjugation of that vehicle at sea and on land.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it is that one says: "Praise be to Allah, who provided me with this and carried me upon it." ﴿And say, "Exalted is He who has subjected this to us"﴾: that is, He made this vehicle submissive to us. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib read: "Exalted is He who subjected this to us."

Qatada said: He has taught you how to say when you ride.

The meaning of ﴿And we were not able to control it﴾ is: we were not capable of it. It is said: "aqrana hadhā al-baʿīr" when he was able to control it. Al-Akhfash and Abu ʿUbayda said: "muqrinīn" means controlling. It was said: equal to it in strength, from their saying: "he is the qirn of so-and-so" when he is like him in strength. Qutrub recited the verse of ʿAmr ibn Maʿdi Karib:

"Indeed the tribes know that ʿUqayl has for us, in calamities, none who controls us."

Another said:

"You rode the two difficult mounts of recklessness and cowardice, and you are not ones who can master the difficult."

The meaning of "al-anʿam" here is camels specifically; it was said: camels and cattle, and the first is preferable.

﴿And indeed to our Lord we will surely return﴾: that is, we will return to Him. This is the completion of what is said upon mounting a beast or a ship.

Then He returned — glory be to Him — to mention the disbelievers who were previously mentioned, and said: ﴿And they have attributed to Him from His servants a portion﴾. Qatada said: that is, an equal, meaning whatever is worshipped besides Allah.

Al-Zajjaj and al-Mubarrad said: "al-juzʾ" here means daughters, and "al-juzʾ" among the people of Arabic means daughters; it is said: "qad ajza'at al-mar'a" when the woman bore daughters. From it is the saying of the poet:

"If a free woman has given birth to daughters one day, there is no wonder; a free woman may sometimes bear males, sometimes the opposite."

The author of al-Kashshaf considered explaining "al-juzʾ" as daughters to be among the innovations of tafsir, and declared it a lie upon the Arabs.

This can be answered: al-Zajjaj and al-Mubarrad narrated it, and they are the two imams of the Arabic language, its preservers, and the ultimate authorities in knowledge of it. And what will come later supports explaining "al-juzʾ" as daughters, His saying: ﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates?﴾, and His saying: ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful﴾, and His saying: ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾. It was also said: what is meant by "al-juzʾ" here is the angels, for they made them children of Allah, glory be to Him; this was said by Mujahid and al-Hasan.

Al-Azhari said: the meaning of the verse is that they made for Allah a portion of His servants, meaning: they made Allah's share of offspring. ﴿Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful﴾: that is, manifestly ungrateful and exaggerated in it. It was said: what is meant by "al-insān" here is the disbeliever, for he is the one who denies Allah's blessings upon him with clear denial.

Then He denounced them for this, saying: ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen for you sons?﴾ This is an interrogation of reproach and rebuke.

"Am" here is the disjunctive "am," and the meaning is: has your Lord taken daughters for Himself, and chosen sons for you? So He made for Himself the lesser of the two categories, and for you the more excellent of them. It is said: "aṣfaytuhu bi-kadhā," meaning: I preferred him with it; and "aṣfaytuhu al-wudd," meaning: I made the affection pure for him. Similar to this verse is His saying: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That would be an unjust division﴾ [al-Najm: 21], and His saying: ﴿Has your Lord then chosen you with sons?﴾ [al-Isra': 40]. The clause "wa-aṣfākum" is conjoined to "ittakhadha," and falls with it under the denial.

Then He increased their reproach and rebuke, saying: ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as an example﴾: that is, of what He ascribed to the Most Merciful, glory be to Him, of having taken daughters for Himself. The meaning is that when one of them is given good news that a daughter has been born to him, he is grieved by it and its effect appears on him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿his face becomes dark﴾, that is, his face becomes black because of the birth of a female to him, when what was born to him was not a male in its place. ﴿And he is filled with suppressed grief﴾: that is, intensely grieving, greatly distressed, full of it.

Qatada said: "grieved." ʿIkrimah said: "distressed." It was said: "silent." The clause ﴿and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾ is in the place of accusative as a circumstance.

Then He increased their reproach and rebuke, saying: ﴿Is one who is brought up in ornaments, and who in dispute is not clear?﴾ The meaning of "yunashsha'" is "yurabbā" (is raised), and "al-nushū'" is upbringing, and "al-ḥilya" is adornment. The "man" is in the accusative place by an implied governing verb conjoined to "ja'alū," and the meaning is: "Did they make for Him — glory be to Him — one who is raised in adornment, while he is incapable of managing his own affairs, and when he is disputed with, he cannot establish his argument or repel what his opponent argues against him, due to deficiency of intellect and weakness of judgment?"

Al-Mubarrad said: the estimated sense of the verse is: "Or do they attribute to Him one who grows up in adornment," meaning: one who grows in ornament.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read *yunsha'u* with a fatha on the *ya'* and a sukun on the *nun*. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, Ibn Wathhab, Hafs, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with a damma on the *ya'*, a fatha on the *nun* and a shaddah on the *shin*.

Abu Hatim preferred the first reading (*qira'ah*, recitation), and Abu 'Ubayd preferred the second.

Al-Harawi said: On the first reading the verb is intransitive (*lazim*), and on the second it is transitive (*muta'addin*). The meaning is: she is brought up and grows up among ornaments (*al-hilyah*).

Qatadah said: "A woman rarely speaks with her argument without speaking with the argument against herself." Ibn Zayd and al-Dahhak said: What is "brought up among ornaments" refers to their idols, which they fashioned from gold and silver.

﴿And they made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females.﴾ The word *ja'l* (making, or ascribing) here means saying and passing a judgment on a thing, as when you say: "I made Zayd the best of people," meaning: you said this and judged him to be so.

The Kufans read *'ibad* (servants) in the plural, and Ibn 'Abbas also read it this way. The rest read *'inda al-Rahman* (with the Most Merciful), with a sukun on the *nun*. Abu 'Ubayd preferred the first reading, because the chain of attribution (*al-isnad*) is higher in it, and because Allah only refuted them in their statement that they are the daughters of Allah (p-1337), so He informed them that they are His servants. This reading is supported by His words: ﴿Rather, they are honoured servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26]. Abu Hatim preferred the second reading and said: Confirmation of this reading is His words: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ [al-A'raf 206].

Then He rebuked and reproached them, saying: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ That is, were they present at Allah's creation of them? This is from *shahadah* in the sense of presence (*huduur*). In this there is mockery of them and a declaration of their ignorance.

The majority read *ashahidu* as an interrogative without a waw. Nafi' read *awa-shahidu* (with a waw).

The majority read *satuktabu shahadatuhum* (their testimony will be recorded), with a damma on the *ta'* and the verb in the passive, and *shahadatuhum* in the nominative. Al-Sulami, Ibn al-Sumayfa' and Hubayrah from Hafs read it with a *nun* and the verb in the active, with *shahadatahum* in the accusative. Abu Raja' read *shahadatuhum* in the plural. The meaning: We shall record this testimony that they gave in the register of their deeds, so that We may recompense them for it, and they will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And they said: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them."﴾ This is another kind of their disbelief in Allah, which they brought out for mockery and ridicule. Its meaning: If the Most Merciful had willed, in your supposition, we would not have worshipped these angels. This is a true statement by which falsehood is intended, and its explanation has already passed in al-An'am. Then He, glory be to Him, exposed their ignorance by His words: ﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾, that is: they have no knowledge of what they said, that if Allah willed that they not worship the angels, they would not have worshipped them. Rather, they spoke of it out of ignorance, intending by what has the form of truth something false, and they supposed that whatever He wills, He is pleased with.

Then He made clear the absence of their knowledge by His words: ﴿They are only guessing﴾, that is: they are only lying in what they said, and fabricating a vain excuse.

It was said that the reference in His words "that" (*dhalika*) is to His words: ﴿And they made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females.﴾ This was said by Qatadah, Muqatil and al-Kalbi. Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: That is, they have no knowledge concerning the worship of idols.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The first thing Allah created was the pen, and He commanded it to write what will be until the Day of Resurrection, and the Book is with Him. Then he recited: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you altogether?﴾ He said: Do you wish that it be withheld from you, and you did not do what you were commanded?

Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he travelled, would mount his riding beast, then say *Allahu akbar* three times, then say: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿And we could not have subdued it﴾ that he said: "Capable of it" (*mutiqin*).

'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted from him concerning ﴿Is one brought up among ornaments...﴾ that he said: It refers to women. He distinguished between their dress and the dress of men, deprived them of inheritance and testimony, commanded them to remain seated, and named them *al-khawalif* (those who stay behind).

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: I used to read this word: ﴿Who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾, so I asked Ibn 'Abbas, and he said: "Servants of the Most Merciful?" I said: In my copy of the Qur'an it is "with the Most Merciful" (*'inda al-Rahman*). He said: Erase it and write it as "servants of the Most Merciful."

* *

(p-1361) It is a Meccan surah. Al-Qurtubi said: This is the view of all of them. Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that they both said: The surah *Ha-Mim al-Ahqaf* was revealed in Mecca.

Ibn al-Durays and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me the surah of al-Ahqaf, and another man taught it differently from my recitation. I said: Who taught you it? He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me something other than this. So we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and I said: O Messenger of Allah, did you not teach me such-and-such? He said: Yes. And the other said: Did you not teach me such-and-such? He said: Yes. Then the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed, and he said: Let each of you recite what he has heard, for those before you were destroyed only by disagreement."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

His words: 1. ﴿Ha Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ This has already been discussed fully in the surah of Ghafir and what follows it. We mentioned the grammatical analysis (*wajh al-i'rab*) and the explanation of what is the truth: that the opening letters of the surahs belong to the *mutashabih* (the ambiguous verses), whose knowledge must be left to the One who sent it down.

﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾ of all created things, in their entirety, except with truth. This is an exceptive phrase (*istithna' mufarragh*) from the most general of states, that is: except as a creation bound with the truth which the divine will requires. His words ﴿and for a specified term﴾ are coordinated with "the truth": that is, except with the truth, and for a specified term, by supposing an omitted noun: that is, and by appointing a specified term. This term is the Day of Resurrection, when the heavens and the earth and what is between them will come to an end, and the earth will be replaced by another earth and the heavens.

It was said that the specified term means the end of the term of each individual created thing. The first view is preferable. This indicates the Hour's arrival and the termination of the duration of this world, and that Allah did not create His creation in vain and for no purpose, but created it for reward and punishment. ﴿But those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of﴾, that is: from what they were warned and frightened of in the Qur'an, of resurrection, reckoning and recompense; they are turning away, avoiding it, not preparing for it. The clause is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), meaning: while they are turning away from it, not believing in it. The "*ma*" in His words "what they are warned of" may be a relative pronoun, or it may be a verbal-noun (*masdariyyah*) "ma".

﴿Say: Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah?﴾ That is: tell me what you worship besides Allah, of idols. ﴿Show me what they have created of the earth﴾, that is: what thing they created from it. His words "show me" may be an emphasis on His words "have you considered": that is, tell me, show me, and the second object of "have you considered" is "what they created." It may also not be an emphasis, but this may be a case of *tanazu'* (competition between two verbs for one object), since "have you considered" requires a second object and "show me" does too. ﴿Or do they have a partnership in the heavens?﴾ This "or" is the disjunctive *am*, presumed to mean "rather" plus the interrogative hamzah. The meaning: Rather, do they have a partnership with Allah in them? The interrogation is for reproach and rebuke.

﴿Bring me a Book before this﴾. This is a rebuke for them and a demonstration of their inability and incapacity to bring the like of it. The reference in "this" is to the Qur'an, for it has clearly declared the falsehood of association (*shirk*), that Allah is One with no partner, and that the Hour is true with no doubt about it. So is there for the polytheists any book that contradicts this Book, or any proof that opposes this proof?

﴿Or some trace of knowledge﴾. In *al-Sihah*, it is said: "*aw athara min 'ilm*" means a remnant of it, and likewise *al-athrah* with a vowelled *tha'*.

Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, a remnant of the knowledge of the earlier people.

Al-Farra' and al-Mubarrad said: it means what is transmitted from the books of the earlier people.

Al-Wahidi said: This is the meaning of the words of the exegetes.

'Ata' said: or something you transmit from a prophet who came before Muhammad (ﷺ).

Muqatil said: or a narration of knowledge from the prophets.

Al-Zajjaj said: "*aw athara*" means a sign. *Al-athara* is a verbal noun like *al-samahah* (generosity) and *al-shaja'ah* (courage). The root of the word is from *athar* (trace), which is a narration. One says: *athartu al-hadith, uthiruhu, athrah, athara*, and *athran*, when you relate it from another.

The majority read *athara* as a verbal noun, like *al-samahah* and *al-ghawayah* (misguidance). Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, 'Ikrimah, al-Sulami, al-Hasan and Abu Raja' read it with a fatha on the hamzah and the tha', without an alif. Al-Kisa'i read *uthrah* with a damma on the hamzah and a sukun on the tha'.

﴿If you are truthful﴾ in your claim that you make, which is your saying that Allah has a partner. You have brought nothing of this, so the falsity of their statement is established by the rational and transmitted proofs against it.

﴿And who is more astray than one who invokes, besides Allah, those who will not answer him?﴾ That is: there is no one more astray than him, nor more ignorant. For he invokes what does not hear, so how can he hope for an answer, let alone for bringing benefit or repelling harm? Thus it becomes clear that he (p-1362) is the most ignorant of the ignorant and the most astray of the astray. The interrogation is for reproach and rebuke. His words ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾ are the limit of their not answering.

﴿And they are heedless of their invocation﴾. The first pronoun refers to the idols, and the second to their worshippers. The meaning: the idols they invoke are heedless of their invocation of them. They do not hear and do not understand, because they are inanimate objects. The plural in both pronouns is in view of the meaning of "*man*" (whoever). The worshippers of idols applied to the idols what applies to rational beings, because the polytheists believed that the idols understand.

﴿And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and deniers of their worship﴾. That is: when the people who worshipped the idols are gathered, the idols will be enemies to them, disowning one another and cursing one another. It has been said that Allah will create life in the idols, and they will deny them.

It was also said that the meaning is that they deny them and oppose them by the tongue of their state, not by the tongue of speech.

As for the angels, Jesus, 'Uzayr and the devils, they will disown those who worshipped them on the Day of Resurrection, as in His words: ﴿We disown You; they did not used to worship us﴾ [al-Qasas 63]. ﴿And they will be disbelievers in their worship﴾, that is: those who were worshipped by the polytheists would be disbelievers in their worship, that is, deniers and rejecters. It was said that the pronoun in "they will be" refers to the worshippers, as in His words: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am 23]. The first view is preferable.
